כ"ד כסלו EREV CHANUKAH Dear Diary, It’s Chanukah tonight, and I must catch you up! After the Yud-Tes and Chof Kislev farbrengens that I told you about, chassidim got right to work. The first thing they needed to do was buy menorahs to give out. They tried asking different stores and companies, but none of them had enough menorahs, and it would be impossible to make them in time. This mivtza was launched so soon before Chanukah! Not only that, but there is also a metal shortage. (“Shortage” is a new word I learned. It means there isn’t enough of something.) So factories could hardly make any menorahs, even if they wanted to! I didn’t know we’re having a metal shortage now. Did you? Anyways, a neis happened, and the chassidim found a Jewish man named Tibor Kupferstein who owns a factory. Mr. Kupferstein’s factory normally makes supplies for the American army, but he agreed to pause everything in order to make 10,000 lightweight menorahs! His factory has already begun making menorahs 24 hours a day! When Tzach reported this to the Rebbe, the Rebbe responded in pleasant surprise, “Ten thousand?!” I hope I get to give out some of these menorahs tonight! Love, Yehudis P.S. The Rebbe wrote a Chanukah letter especially for us kids under bar and bas mitzvah, and told us that by lighting the menorah in the proper way, we show others how important the mitzvah is! The

Mivtzoim—they feel like they’ve been around forever! Can you even imagine life without them? Yet, unbelievably, before the Rebbe introduced each of the mitzvah campaigns that we know so well, they simply didn’t exist.

Join us as we explore imaginary old diaries that could have belonged to kids just like you— kids who might have lived during the time when the Rebbe first announced many of these mivtzoim.

Read this 52-year-old diary written by a girl named Yehudis (who was just ten years old at the time), and watch as the beginnings of Mivtza Chanukah light up for you, too! )1973( כ' כסלו, תשל"ד

MOTZEI SHABBOS Dear Diary, What a rollercoaster of a year this has been, and it’s barely begun! First there was the war, which you know already … I wrote so much about the surprise attack on Eretz Yisroel that happened on Yom Kippur. At first, we were petrified, and then we saw incredible nissim. And now this! A new mivtza! Let me backtrack. Thursday night, Friday, and Shabbos have been packed with Yud-Tes and Chof Kislev celebrations. During the farbrengens, the Rebbe started talking about the next exciting Yom Tov—Chanukah! The Rebbe declared that we must help other Yidden celebrate, and that there should be at least one menorah per house. “If you meet anyone who doesn’t have a menorah, you should give one to them. And it would also be good that every child lights their own menorah,” the Rebbe said. Wow! To knock on people’s doors and bring Chanukah to them? I’ve never heard of such a thing! Mommy excitedly told us at our family’s Melave Malka that it shows how much the Rebbe cares for and remembers every single Yid. Which reminds me: The Rebbe also said that in Eretz Yisroel, there should be a menorah at every army base and watchtower, even if just one soldier is stationed there. Just one! Plus, chassidim are to visit the homes of widows, orphans, and wounded soldiers, so they, too, can feel the light of Chanukah. The Rebbe ended the Shabbos farbrengen by saying that a meeting should be held right after havdalah to start making plans. There’s no time to waste. Chanukah is just four nights away! Love, Yehudis

On Zos Chanukah, the Rebbe called for a special Chanukah rally for kids! My friends and I all went.

Plus, that night, there was a surprise farbrengen! The Rebbe said that the Chanukah pe’ulos were super successful, and everyone should say “l’chaim". The Rebbe even sent wine & mezonos to the ladies section because we were very involved, too!

On Shabbos afternoon, I visited my friend Fraida’s house, and her tatty told us that Tzach had to keep asking Mr. Kupferstein for more and more menorahs. By the end of Chanukah, 60,000 were given out! That’s enough menorahs for almost 1,300 school buses filled with kids!

After being busy with menorahs for days on end, I’ll bet Mr. Kupferstein also dreams about menorahs at night!

Anyone over bar and bas mitzvah who went on mivtzoim was allowed to get, and gelt was even sent to Eretz Yisroel!

Don’t forget, dear diary, that hardly anyone gets a dollar or coin from the Rebbe, so it was a very special thing!

My parents are going to frame their Chanukah gelt to remind the whole family how important Mivtza Chanukah is to the Rebbe.

You definitely need an update on how this new mivtza is going!

Since the minute Chanukah began, chassidim have been in high gear. Busloads of bochurim and tatties have been pouring out of 770 and driving all over to spread the light of Chanukah. They’ve been visiting people in their homes, going to businesses, and giving out menorahs in the streets.

I went with my mother and sisters to Manhattan, and gave out 14 menorahs that Mr. Kupferstein made! People just love Chanukah, and are so excited when we offer them these menorahs.

And get this: Someone had a wild idea to put a menorah on top of a car! So they built one and parked the car in front of 770. When the Rebbe saw it, he told them to light it! A car menorah- -imagine that! Later, bochurim drove it to Fifth Avenue in Manhattan for more mivtzoim. One night, the mayor of New York, Mr. John Lindsay, came to see it. As the newspaper cameras took pictures, he gave each bochur a handshake.

Can you imagine? It was in the newspapers! The whole city saw the light of Chanukah!
